answer: In a market where AI agents trade walnut, cedar, and other timber, each agent must lock a $100 bond before submitting bids. A bond cannot back two active identities and stays locked for 30 days after the last bid. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up $100,000 for at least a month, even if generating their keys is free. The defense makes influence costly: every extra bidding identity requires additional capital that the attacker cannot spend elsewhere.
